question: Why did a suntan switch from a mark of poverty to a mark of wealth in the twentieth century?
answer: Because the kind of work changed. While most poor people laboured in fields, pale skin proved you did not; once they moved into factories and offices, a tan proved you had the time and money for sun and holidays. In the 1920s fashion took it up, and bronze became a luxury.
move: A status symbol is whatever most people find hard to get.
ask: Which thing I envy is really just whatever happens to be hard to get right now?
reference: Kerry Segrave, Suntanning in 20th Century America, McFarland, 2005
